question: Which of the following is considered a common vehicle for disease transmission?

options.A: Air currents in a closed hospital room
options.B: Direct skin-to-skin touch with a patient
options.C: A mosquito bite during the evening hours
options.D: Contaminated drinking water supplies

explanation: Water, food, and blood are common vehicles capable of carrying pathogens to a large group of people simultaneously. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main way Metformin helps lower blood sugar in the body?

options.A: Stimulating the beta cells of the pancreas to release stored insulin
options.B: Slowing down the digestion of carbohydrates in the small intestine
options.C: Decreasing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity
options.D: Blocking the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules

explanation: Exactly right! Metformin tells the liver to ease up on making extra sugar and helps your body's cells respond better to your natural insulin.

question: What do we call health issues that linger for weeks or months after recovering from COVID-19?

options.A: Acute rebound syndrome
options.B: Secondary convalescence
options.C: Long COVID
options.D: Delayed viral shedding

explanation: When symptoms stick around long after the initial infection is gone, it's known as Long COVID. You're making steady progress! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h6)

question: When preparing a weaker cream from a stronger stock, what is your very first step?

options.A: Identify the starting strength and your target strength
options.B: Measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output
options.C: Throw away half of the total stock bottle immediately
options.D: Add water directly into the manufacturer's original tube

explanation: Always check where you are starting (stock strength) and where you want to end up before doing any math!

question: In Superior Mesenteric Artery syndrome, what actually squeezes or traps the duodenum?

options.A: Compression of the bowel between the aorta and a major artery
options.B: A large benign tumor growing inside the intestinal lining
options.C: Severe twisting of the small intestine around its own blood supply
options.D: Scar tissue buildup following multiple abdominal surgeries

explanation: That's correct! When protective fat is lost, the superior mesenteric artery can press down and trap part of the duodenum right against the big aorta.

question: What is a major reason for giving a neuromuscular blocker during emergency intubation?

options.A: To relax vocal cords and jaw muscles for safe tube placement
options.B: To help the patient clear thick mucus secretions from the lungs
options.C: To stimulate the patient to breathe deeply on their own without help
options.D: To instantly reverse dangerous drops in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Relaxing the jaw and vocal cords makes sliding the breathing tube in much smoother, protecting the patient's airway and throat from trauma.

question: A nurse checks a patient's pedal pulses and finds the left pulse is strong while the right pulse cannot be felt at all. What is the most immediate clinical concern?

options.A: High blood pressure throughout the body
options.B: A potential blockage in the right leg artery
options.C: An allergic reaction to heart medication
options.D: A normal variation in elderly patients

explanation: An absent pulse on only one side strongly suggests local arterial occlusion or injury, requiring urgent follow-up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which professional group acts as the primary defense against prescribing and dosage errors before drugs reach the ward?

options.A: Medical records clerks
options.B: Ward porters
options.C: Pharmacists
options.D: Hospital accountants

explanation: Pharmacists review the initial orders and verify clinical safety before preparing the individual doses for distribution. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the best bed position to set a patient in before you feed them?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 30 degrees
options.D: 15 degrees

explanation: Sitting them straight up (High Fowler's at 90 degrees) lets gravity do the hard work, pulling food safely down the esophagus instead of toward the airway.

question: When planning a new health program in a village, why is it vital for a nurse to involve local leaders?

options.A: To shift all financial responsibility onto the community members
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: To comply with international travel regulations
options.D: To ensure the program respects local values and gains community acceptance

explanation: Well done! Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure your health projects fit nicely with the culture and lifestyle of the people.

question: What is the normal pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Keep this number locked in your memory! A pH of 7.35 to 7.45 keeps body enzymes working smoothly and cells happy.

question: Why don't diaphragms and cervical caps protect very well against skin-to-skin STIs like HPV?

options.A: They leave the vaginal walls and external skin exposed
options.B: They allow semen to leak freely around the sides of the device
options.C: They dissolve too quickly when exposed to bodily fluids
options.D: They absorb viral particles and push them directly into the uterus

explanation: Correct! Because they only cover the cervix, surrounding skin and vaginal walls are still exposed to touch-based viruses. Great clinical insight!

question: Why is fighting social stigma just as important as giving medicine when dealing with airborne diseases?

options.A: Social isolation changes the physical structure of droplet nuclei
options.B: Community rumors replace the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: Fear of discrimination often causes patients to delay seeking care
options.D: Stigma directly inactivates the bacteria inside the lungs

explanation: So true! When people are afraid of being judged or stigmatized, they hide their sickness and stay away from clinics, which unfortunately lets the disease spread further.

question: What is a top clinical priority when caring for a patient mid-flight?

options.A: Adjusting the aircraft navigation controls
options.B: Maintaining airway security and hemodynamic stability
options.C: Serving meals and beverages to the transport crew
options.D: Completing billing forms before landing

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Keeping the airway clear and vital signs stable will always be your number one duty in any critical transport.

question: Why do public health experts say that most maternal deaths are preventable?

options.A: Because traditional herbs can cure all pregnancy issues
options.B: Because pregnant women rarely develop severe complications
options.C: Because pregnancy complications always give weeks of warning
options.D: Because effective medical treatments and interventions exist

explanation: Spot on! With good antenatal care, skilled birth attendants, and quick emergency care, we can successfully manage and stop most life-threatening complications.

question: What is 'hungry bone syndrome', which can happen right after a parathyroidectomy?

options.A: Remodeled bones rapidly take up calcium and phosphate to rebuild their structure.
options.B: The surgical incision causes temporary starvation and loss of appetite.
options.C: The remaining parathyroid glands instantly shut down all hormone production.
options.D: The kidneys suddenly stop filtering waste products from the bloodstream.

explanation: Once high PTH is suddenly removed, starved bones eagerly soak up calcium from the blood to rebuild themselves, causing blood calcium to drop fast!

question: In the ABCDE primary survey, what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Drainage
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: D is for Disability! It is just a quick check of the patient's neurological status and brain function.

question: Which plant is the natural source of the heart medication digoxin?

options.A: Opium poppy plant
options.B: Digitalis or foxglove
options.C: Deadly nightshade
options.D: Cinchona tree bark

explanation: Digoxin comes from the pretty foxglove plant! It's a classic example of how nature helps us treat heart conditions.

question: What Nigerian legislation explicitly bans the practice of Female Genital Mutilation nationwide?

options.A: The National Minimum Wage Decree
options.B: The Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: The Federal Highway Safety Regulation
options.D: The Environmental Sanitation Edict

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: To eliminate all potential discomforts of pregnancy
options.B: To prevent the fetus from moving into a breech position
options.C: To detect silent conditions like high blood pressure early
options.D: To guarantee a normal vaginal delivery date

explanation: You got it! Some dangerous issues like high blood pressure don't show early signs, which is why regular clinic checks are so important.

question: High blood pressure, protein in the urine, and sudden swelling during pregnancy are classic warning signs of:

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placenta previa
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Great job! Preeclampsia is a serious pregnancy condition marked by high BP and protein in the urine that requires quick medical attention.

question: A community nurse visits a patient with psychosis who looks very suspicious and guarded. What is the best first move?

options.A: Start with calm, non-threatening social conversation before asking clinical questions
options.B: Confront the client about their false beliefs right away to establish reality
options.C: Immediately demand a urine sample to check for illicit drug use
options.D: Leave the home immediately without assessing to avoid agitation

explanation: Brilliant! Taking it slow and building a friendly rapport helps lower anxiety so the patient feels safe enough to talk.

question: Which service would you most expect to find at a local primary health care center?

options.A: Sub-specialty pediatric neurology consultations
options.B: Advanced cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy
options.C: Routine childhood immunization and antenatal care
options.D: Complex open-heart surgical procedures

explanation: Primary health centers focus heavily on community wellness. That means giving babies their routine vaccines and supporting mothers with antenatal care every day!

question: In the Three Delays Model for maternal mortality, what does the second delay mean?

options.A: Postponing antenatal care visits until the third trimester of pregnancy
options.B: Reaching a functioning health facility due to transport and distance problems
options.C: Deciding whether or not to leave the home when labor contractions start
options.D: Waiting for doctors to arrive at the hospital after the patient has registered

explanation: The second delay is all about logistics—navigating bad roads, lack of vehicles, and long distances to get a patient to a clinic or hospital. Spot-on!

question: What does the term ageism mean in healthcare?

options.A: The natural physical decline of body organs over time
options.B: Prejudice and discrimination based on a person's age
options.C: Specialized nursing care for pediatric and geriatric groups
options.D: Offering free medical care only to senior citizens

explanation: Ageism refers to unfair treatment, stereotypes, and prejudice directed at individuals simply because they are older. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why does a nurse monitor the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for a patient receiving heparin?

options.A: To measure the exact number of active platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: To check if the patient has developed an iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To ensure the intrinsic and common pathways are appropriately suppressed
options.D: To evaluate how well the liver is producing new red blood cells

explanation: Heparin affects the intrinsic pathway, so checking the aPTT lets the nurse know if the drug dose is safe and effective. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why does a pulmonary shunt cause very low blood oxygen that doesn't easily fix with standard oxygen therapy?

options.A: Excess carbon dioxide blocks the hemoglobin binding sites permanently
options.B: Surfactant production stops completely, causing widespread lung collapse
options.C: Blood bypasses unventilated alveoli, so it never gets oxygen to pick up
options.D: The heart pumps too slowly to push blood through the narrowed pulmonary veins

explanation: Exactly. If blood flows past collapsed or fluid-filled sacs without getting oxygen, adding extra oxygen to room air can't reach that blocked blood! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to press hard on the abdomen of a patient who might have a pheochromocytoma?

options.A: It can stimulate excess cortisol release and lower the patient's blood sugar.
options.B: It can permanently damage the kidney and lead to acute renal failure.
options.C: It can rupture the adrenal gland and cause immediate internal bleeding into the abdomen.
options.D: It can trigger a massive release of catecholamines and cause a dangerous hypertensive crisis.

explanation: Pressing on that tumor is like squeezing a tube of toothpaste—it shoots a massive wave of adrenaline into the bloodstream, sending blood pressure dangerously high. Hands off the tummy!

question: What is the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina called?

options.A: The cervix
options.B: The fallopian tube
options.C: The endometrium
options.D: The myometrium

explanation: The cervix forms the lower, narrow portion of the uterus connecting the uterine cavity to the vaginal canal, which is the specific site where cervical cancer originates. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is community education just as important as legal bans when fighting to eliminate FGM?

options.A: Healthcare workers are not allowed to read legal documents
options.B: Community education changes cultural beliefs and tackles the root causes
options.C: Community leaders demand payment to obey the law
options.D: Laws are too expensive to print and distribute

explanation: You got it! While laws set the rules, stopping deep-seated traditions requires educating community members so they choose to leave the practice behind. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h8)

question: What does empowerment mean in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity to solve health problems independently
options.B: Giving financial loans to every household in the village
options.C: Allowing nurses to make all decisions without community input
options.D: Handing out free medicine during festival seasons

explanation: Empowerment equips community members with the skills and confidence to address their own health challenges long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What surgical procedure is often necessary during childbirth for a woman with Type III FGM?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Oophorectomy
options.C: Cervical cerclage
options.D: Defibulation

explanation: Brilliant! Defibulation means carefully cutting open the scar tissue seal so the mother can have a safe delivery and examination.

question: What is the key sign of compartment syndrome that sets it apart from normal broken bone pain?

options.A: Mild aching pain that only occurs when the patient tries to walk
options.B: A gradual itching sensation underneath the plaster cast shell
options.C: Severe pain that is not relieved by standard opioid pain medications
options.D: Complete absence of any pain due to sudden nerve death

explanation: When pain is extreme and doesn't get better even with strong painkillers, think compartment syndrome! It means dangerous pressure is building up inside the muscle compartments.

question: What is the main goal of the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT)?

options.A: To calculate the correct medication dosage for the child
options.B: To perform a rapid, hands-off visual evaluation from the doorway
options.C: To measure the exact blood pressure and temperature
options.D: To listen carefully to heart murmurs with a stethoscope

explanation: You don't even need to touch the child right away! The PAT is a quick, visual tool you can use from the doorway to size up how sick a little one is.

question: A family facing severe poverty marries off their teenage daughter to reduce expenses. What is the long-term economic reality for the girl herself?

options.A: She typically achieves financial independence much earlier than her peers.
options.B: She is guaranteed employment in local community development projects.
options.C: She usually falls deeper into poverty due to lost education and earning potential.
options.D: She gains lifelong financial security through her spouse's extended family.

explanation: Well done! When schooling stops early, girls lose out on future skills and jobs, which often traps them and their future children in a cycle of poverty.

question: Which hormone helps your kidneys save water when your body is dehydrated?

options.A: Anti-diuretic hormone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Think of Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) as your body's 'anti-pee' signal. It tells your kidney collecting ducts to hold onto water so you don't get dehydrated.

question: Which licensing requirement must a tele-nurse always meet when caring for remote clients?

options.A: Holding a valid license in the location where the patient is physically located
options.B: Having a license from any country as long as the nurse has a smartphone
options.C: Possessing a special international internet communication permit
options.D: Registering only with the hospital administration board

explanation: Regulatory bodies require nurses to be legally licensed in the specific jurisdiction where the patient receives the care. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: What is the standard time frame following the end of a pregnancy for a death to be classified as a maternal death?

options.A: Within 6 months
options.B: Within 7 days
options.C: Within 42 days
options.D: Within 1 year

explanation: A maternal death includes any death occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days following the termination of the pregnancy, provided it is related to the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h1)

question: What style of training was mostly used in early Nigerian missionary hospitals?

options.A: Apprenticeship training
options.B: Military conscription
options.C: Online distance learning
options.D: University fellowship

explanation: You got it! Back then, nursing learners picked up practical skills through hands-on work right in the hospital wards, much like learning a trade.

question: A male patient is getting a semen analysis for fertility checks. What should you tell him to do beforehand?

options.A: Avoid eating any protein-rich foods for 48 hours prior to the test
options.B: Keep the semen sample in a house refrigerator until arriving at the clinic
options.C: Collect the sample using ordinary household soap and water for hygiene
options.D: Maintain a period of sexual abstinence for 2 to 5 days before collection

explanation: Correct! A 2 to 5 day window of abstinence helps ensure the sperm count and movement are measured as accurately as possible.

question: Why must a single unit of blood be completely infused within a maximum of four hours?

options.A: To prevent bacterial multiplication in the blood product at room temperature
options.B: To allow the nurse to finish the shift before the bag is empty
options.C: To ensure the patient does not become bored during the procedure
options.D: To prevent the blood from freezing inside the intravenous tubing

explanation: Blood is kept cold for a reason! Once it sits at warm room temperature for too long, bacteria love to multiply in it, which can put the patient at risk for severe infection.

question: How does palliative fatigue differ from normal everyday tiredness?

options.A: It only occurs during the first few hours of the morning
options.B: It can always be cured by eating a high-protein meal
options.C: It is caused strictly by a lack of physical exercise
options.D: It does not improve with rest or a good night's sleep

explanation: Palliative fatigue is a deep, systemic exhaustion rooted in the underlying disease process rather than simple lack of sleep. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h5)

question: What is the job of the cooling unit attached to an oxygen tent?

options.A: Filtering bacteria out of the room air supply
options.B: Preventing the inside of the tent from becoming too hot
options.C: Increasing the pressure of oxygen inside the canopy
options.D: Freezing the oxygen gas into liquid form for storage

explanation: Because plastic tents trap body heat and humidity, the cooling unit is essential to keep the little patient comfortable and cool.

question: How do secondary causes differ from primary causes of nephrotic conditions?

options.A: Secondary causes always resolve completely without medication
options.B: Secondary causes only affect adults over the age of sixty
options.C: Primary causes involve infections outside the urinary tract
options.D: Secondary causes are systemic diseases that damage the kidneys as a complication

explanation: You're doing great! Think of primary causes as starting right in the kidney, while secondary causes happen when a whole-body condition like diabetes or lupus ends up hurting the kidneys along the way.

question: As a nurse, what is the best first step before handing out a sleeping pill?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity in bright sunlight
options.B: Administering a cup of strong coffee to test drug interactions
options.C: Requiring the patient to sign a legal release form
options.D: Assessing the underlying cause of insomnia and trying sleep hygiene measures

explanation: Always check why they can't sleep and try natural comfort tips first before reaching straight for the prescription pad!

question: A nurse accidentally touches a patient's eyelid with the tip of an eye drop bottle. What is the safest action to take?

options.A: Wipe the tip with a dry tissue and keep using it
options.B: Discard the bottle to prevent spreading infection
options.C: Rinse the bottle tip under hot tap water
options.D: Store the bottle in the refrigerator for twenty-four hours

explanation: Once a dropper tip touches a patient, it is considered contaminated and should not be used again to avoid infection. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h3)

question: A patient died with an IV line in place and a coroner's post-mortem is requested. What should the nurse do with the line?

options.A: Hide the lines under the bedsheets
options.B: Remove all lines immediately to clean the skin
options.C: Leave all lines and tubes in place
options.D: Cut the tubing short and tape it down

explanation: For coroner's cases or potential legal investigations, invasive lines and tubes must be left intact for the pathologist. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following is a key performance indicator used to evaluate directing effectiveness?

options.A: The physical color of the walls in the hospital ward
options.B: Medication error rates and patient satisfaction scores
options.C: The brand of uniforms worn by junior nursing staff
options.D: The total number of chairs in the nurse's lounge

explanation: Quality indicators like error rates and patient feedback directly reflect how well guidance and management are working on the floor. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h8)

question: What is the main goal of setting short-term targets for a patient with a metabolic disorder?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future nursing assessments
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying chronic endocrine disease
options.C: To achieve immediate stabilization of dangerous lab values
options.D: To replace the physician's medical treatment orders

explanation: Correct! Short-term goals are all about stepping back from the edge—like pulling a patient away from dangerously high or low blood sugar right now.

question: What structural feature makes capillaries ideally suited for gas and nutrient exchange?

options.A: They are equipped with one-way valves to prevent backflow
options.B: Their walls are only a single cell layer thick
options.C: They contain strong layers of circular smooth muscle
options.D: Their lumen has a larger diameter than any other vessel

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells to start producing testosterone?

options.A: Androgen-binding protein
options.B: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.C: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Luteinizing hormone (LH) travels from your brain's pituitary gland down to the testes, giving Leydig cells the green light to make testosterone.

question: What is a top nursing priority right after a reproductive surgery like a hysterectomy?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake for the first 48 hours
options.B: Monitoring vital signs closely for signs of hemorrhage or infection
options.C: Preventing the patient from moving or walking for a week
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to free up hospital beds

explanation: Spot on! Right after surgery, keeping a close eye on vitals helps you catch early warning signs of bleeding or infection.

question: What electrolyte abnormality is a key feature of Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: High potassium
options.B: Low phosphate
options.C: High calcium
options.D: Low sodium

question: Why is a fever in a neutropenic patient considered a medical emergency?

options.A: It causes severe bleeding that is impossible to stop
options.B: A compromised immune system means a mild infection can rapidly turn fatal
options.C: It always causes permanent paralysis in the legs
options.D: It instantly stops the kidneys from producing any urine

explanation: Without enough white blood cells to fight back, a small fever can quickly become overwhelming. Quick action with antibiotics saves lives here!

question: Why does blood pressure fall in early and mid-pregnancy even though blood volume is rising?

options.A: Kidneys excrete all excess fluid immediately
options.B: The heart pumps with much less force
options.C: Blood vessels constrict to push blood to the lungs
options.D: Progesterone reduces systemic vascular resistance

question: If someone accidentally gets a corrosive chemical in their eyes or on their skin, what is the recommended minimum time to flush it with clean water?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 15 minutes
options.C: Until the burning stops
options.D: One full hour

explanation: You nailed it! Flushing continuously for at least 15 minutes is crucial to dilute the chemical and wash it away before it burns deep into the tissue.

question: How many patient identifiers should a nurse check before giving a medication?

options.A: At least two identifiers
options.B: Three separate room numbers
options.C: Four family member approvals
options.D: Only one quick identifier

explanation: Using identifiers like the patient's name and hospital number ensures the right person receives the treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which hormone tells your kidneys to hold onto water by opening special channels in the collecting ducts?

options.A: Antidiuretic hormone
options.B: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Atrial natriuretic peptide
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Spot on! ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) steps in when you are low on fluids to make sure you don't pee away your precious water.

question: Who is known as the father of nutrition for his early work on how our bodies use oxygen to burn food for energy?

options.A: James Lind
options.B: Casimir Funk
options.C: Antoine Lavoisier
options.D: Hippocrates

explanation: Correct! Lavoisier used clever chemical experiments to show how respiration and metabolism tie directly into how we process food.

question: What is the primary function of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Storing long-term memories in the brain
options.B: Regulating involuntary body functions
options.C: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscles
options.D: Processing conscious thoughts and logic

explanation: The autonomic nervous system works automatically to control internal organs and involuntary processes without conscious effort. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h1)

question: If you visit a home and suspect a vulnerable client is being abused, what is your primary duty?

options.A: Wait until you have absolute proof before telling anyone
options.B: Confront the suspected family member aggressively during the visit
options.C: Report your suspicion immediately to the proper protective authorities
options.D: Keep it a secret to protect family relationships

explanation: Correct! When dealing with vulnerable clients, your priority is their safety. Report suspicions right away so the right agencies can step in.

question: What is the main goal of passing an endotracheal tube during resuscitation?

options.A: To secure a direct passage for oxygen into the lungs
options.B: To remove fluid directly from the stomach
options.C: To prevent the patient from speaking to staff
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the patient

explanation: An endotracheal tube creates a safe, clear highway straight into the lungs, bypassing any blockages in the upper airway.

question: Why is measuring hourly urine output so important when monitoring a bleeding patient?

options.A: It is a reliable indicator of whether vital organs are receiving enough blood
options.B: It prevents the urinary bladder from becoming overstretched
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact blood type of the patient
options.D: It proves that the patient is drinking enough water by mouth

explanation: The kidneys are sensitive to drops in blood volume; if urine output falls, it means perfusion to major organs is inadequate. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h4)

question: Why should a surgical knot be positioned to the side of the wound incision rather than directly over it?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to pull out later
options.B: To prevent pressure on the wound line that can slow healing
options.C: To ensure the local anesthetic stays active longer
options.D: To save suture material during the procedure

explanation: Placing knots off-center prevents direct pressure and irritation on the healing skin edge underneath. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: What does a 'cycloplegic' drug do when dropped into the eye?

options.A: Increases the drainage of fluid from the eye chambers
options.B: Constricts the pupil down to a tiny pinpoint size
options.C: Numbs the surface of the cornea for a quick check
options.D: Paralyzes the focusing muscle inside the eye

question: Beyond physical checks, what is another crucial part of postpartum care for a mother who just had twins or triplets?

options.A: Encouraging the mother to return to work within two weeks
options.B: Restricting family visits to prevent the mother from talking
options.C: Providing emotional support and connecting them with practical resources
options.D: Insisting that the mother cares for the newborns entirely on her own

explanation: Well done! Raising more than one baby at once can feel overwhelming. Offering kind words and connecting families to helper networks is a huge part of great nursing care.

question: Which piece of bedside equipment is a must-have when giving mouth care to an unresponsive patient?

options.A: Hard wooden tongue blades
options.B: A sharp dental mirror probe
options.C: Working suction machine
options.D: Strong alcoholic mouthwash

explanation: Unconscious patients can't spit or swallow water on their own. Having a suction machine ready is vital to clear out liquids and prevent choking.

question: How soon can a person's fertility return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: After exactly six months
options.B: Not for at least two years
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Only after menopause begins

explanation: Surprise! Ovulation can bounce back in as little as two weeks. That's why talking about family planning early is so crucial before she leaves the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of using an arterial line instead of a standard blood pressure cuff?

options.A: It automatically delivers intravenous fluids when pressure drops
options.B: It measures the exact amount of urine produced by the kidneys
options.C: It provides continuous, real-time blood pressure readings
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of infection and bleeding

explanation: An arterial line gives beat-by-beat blood pressure updates, which is super helpful for unstable patients whose numbers change fast.

question: What happens when someone mixes sleeping pills (sedatives) with alcohol?

options.A: Immediate neutralization of all toxic chemicals in the blood
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina and alertness
options.C: Severe respiratory suppression and potential breathing failure
options.D: Enhanced absorption of vital nutrients in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Both alcohol and sedatives slow down the brain. Combining them can make breathing slow down to a dangerous, fatal stop.

question: How does an occupational therapist mostly differ from a physiotherapist?

options.A: Occupational therapists focus on adapting practical daily life tasks and home environments
options.B: Occupational therapists only work in intensive care units
options.C: Occupational therapists are licensed to prescribe medications
options.D: Occupational therapists deal exclusively with mental health disorders

explanation: While physiotherapists focus on body movement and strength, occupational therapists help patients master everyday chores like cooking, washing, and dressing.

question: Which supplement is most important to give before pregnancy to help prevent birth defects?

options.A: Potassium chloride
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin! Taking it before and during early pregnancy greatly lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: How does long-term high blood pressure in the lungs (pulmonary hypertension) directly change the heart?

options.A: It shrinks the left atrium because less blood returns from the lungs
options.B: It causes the heart valves to stretch and leak due to low blood pressure
options.C: It weakens the left ventricle by reducing blood flow through the aorta
options.D: It causes the right ventricle to thicken and enlarge from working too hard

explanation: You've got it! Just like lifting heavy weights makes a bicep grow, the right ventricle bulks up (hypertrophies) when it has to push against high lung pressures. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

options.A: To keep patients admitted in tertiary hospitals for long-term recovery
options.B: To provide acute surgical interventions for physical injuries
options.C: To connect patients with local resources and support for community living
options.D: To isolate individuals with disabilities from the general public

explanation: CBR programs bring rehabilitation and support services directly into the community to help individuals live active, integrated lives. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h7)

question: What actually makes air rush into your lungs when you take an inhalation?

options.A: Intrapulmonary pressure drops below atmospheric pressure
options.B: Surfactant expands the alveolar volume rapidly
options.C: Atmospheric pressure drops below intrapulmonary pressure
options.D: The diaphragm relaxes and pushes the chest upward

explanation: You nailed it! When your chest gets bigger, the pressure inside drops lower than the outside air, sucking air naturally right in.

question: Which model looks at behaviour change as stepping through different stages, like thinking about it, then finally taking action?

options.A: Transtheoretical Model
options.B: Epidemiological Triangle
options.C: Health Belief Model
options.D: Germ Theory of Disease

explanation: Spot on! The Transtheoretical Model helps us understand that change takes time and happens in steady steps.

question: What is usually the main problem with lecturing teenagers about making poor food choices?

options.A: It makes them feel judged and causes them to withdraw from counseling.
options.B: Lectures cause an immediate drop in their blood glucose levels.
options.C: It legally violates their medical privacy rights.
options.D: Teens lack the brain development required to understand nutrition.

explanation: Spot on! Teens hate feeling judged. A friendly, supportive chat builds way more trust than an old-school lecture.

question: What is the primary job of an ascending spinal tract?

options.A: Carrying motor commands down to the muscles
options.B: Carrying sensory information up to the brain
options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid in the spinal canal
options.D: Anchoring the spinal cord to the vertebrae

explanation: Easy to remember: 'ascending' means going up! These tracts act like elevator pathways, taking sensory signals from your body all the way up to the brain.

question: Why is tele-nursing particularly helpful for patients living in remote areas?

options.A: It brings healthcare services directly to homes without requiring travel
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need hospital admission
options.C: It provides free medications delivered straight to the doorstep
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any physical doctor visits

explanation: By using technology, nurses can assess and monitor clients who live far away from physical health facilities. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: How does volunteering to guide and mentor student nurses help a staff nurse grow?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any further hospital training.
options.B: It guarantees an automatic promotion to hospital director.
options.C: It allows the nurse to stop performing direct patient care tasks.
options.D: It builds practical confidence in teaching, guiding, and evaluating others.

explanation: Teaching students is great practice for leadership! It helps you sharpen your communication, build patience, and learn how to guide others effectively.

question: Where do most unsafe abortions and related complications happen around the world?

options.A: In nations where abortion is completely legal on request
options.B: In urban centers with universal healthcare access
options.C: In low- and middle-income countries with restrictive laws
options.D: In countries with high ratios of trained obstetricians

explanation: Spot on! Strict laws paired with weak healthcare systems in developing regions create a high burden of unsafe procedures. Understanding this helps us advocate for better maternal care.

question: A student nurse sees a cleaner throwing used syringes into a normal paper trash bin. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Report the entire ward to the police without speaking to the staff first
options.B: Start throwing all hospital refuse directly out of the ward window
options.C: Ignore the practice since waste disposal is solely the job of orderlies
options.D: Correct the practice immediately, retrain the staff, and ensure proper bins are used

explanation: You got it! As a nurse, you are a safety leader. Educating your team and correcting safety slips right away keeps everyone safe.

question: How can healthcare teams best build resilience in the face of infrastructural challenges?

options.A: Through strong local leadership, protocol adherence, and mutual support
options.B: By ignoring hospital guidelines and working entirely on personal instinct
options.C: By closing down primary health centers permanently during staff shortages
options.D: By refusing to attend to any patient who arrives after working hours

explanation: Resilience in difficult environments is sustained by strong teamwork, adherence to safety standards, and supportive leadership. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h8)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask a fainting patient about visual changes before the event?

options.A: It indicates that permanent blindness is about to occur.
options.B: It helps confirm a vasovagal prodrome rather than sudden cardiac arrest.
options.C: It proves the patient has an underlying eye disease.
options.D: It shows that the patient's blood sugar was extremely high.

explanation: Cardiac syncope usually strikes instantly without warning, whereas vasovagal syncope gives prodromal visual and physical signs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: As a nurse, which assessment finding in a patient's GI check should you report right away?

options.A: Active bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants
options.B: A normal, soft, and non-tender abdomen
options.C: A daily bowel movement of soft consistency
options.D: Blood present in the stool or vomit

explanation: Blood in vomit or stool is a major red flag! It's a sign of bleeding that needs quick medical investigation.

question: A mother says she mixed her child's ORS packet into half a liter of water instead of a full liter. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to add extra sugar to balance out the high salt content
options.B: Instruct her to add another half-liter of water to the existing mixture and stir well
options.C: Allow her to feed the concentrated solution since it will work faster anyway
options.D: Discard the solution and help her mix a fresh batch correctly with one full liter of water

explanation: Guessing water amounts can throw off body chemistry. It is always safest to throw out the wrong mix and prepare a fresh, accurately measured batch.

question: Which hygiene practice should nurses advise patients to avoid to protect their cervix?

options.A: Using scented vaginal douches and chemical sprays
options.B: Washing the external vulva with plain warm water
options.C: Wearing loose-fitting cotton undergarments daily
options.D: Changing sanitary pads frequently during menstruation

explanation: Correct! Douching and scented products mess with the vagina's natural balance and easily irritate delicate tissues.

question: What is the medical term for the warning signs that happen just before a person faints?

options.A: Aura
options.B: Prodrome
options.C: Shock
options.D: Seizure

explanation: The prodrome refers to the early symptoms like sweating and dizziness that signal a faint is coming. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: How much extra stockinette length should generally be cut beyond the planned cast area?

options.A: At least 5 meters for safety
options.B: 10 to 15 centimeters at each end
options.C: Exactly 2 millimeters total
options.D: No extra length at all

explanation: Leaving 10 to 15 centimeters of extra stockinette at both ends is necessary so the edges can be folded back over the cast later. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: What special connections link heart muscle cells together so they can beat in a coordinated rhythm?

options.A: Neuromuscular junctions
options.B: Sarcoplasmic reticula
options.C: Intercalated discs
options.D: Gap-free desmosomes

explanation: Intercalated discs act like special communication highways between heart cells, letting electrical signals pass instantly so the heart pumps as one team!

question: Why is taking rifampicin (for TB) alongside certain HIV drugs tricky?

options.A: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in all patients
options.B: Rifampicin alters liver enzymes and can lower antiretroviral blood levels
options.C: Rifampicin stops the absorption of water in the stomach
options.D: The combination immediately destroys the patient's pancreas

explanation: You got it! Rifampicin speeds up liver enzymes so much that it can flush HIV drugs out of the blood too quickly, risking treatment failure.

question: Which of these is a classic symptom you would expect to see in a patient with severe anemia?

options.A: Rapid and unprovoked weight gain
options.B: Frequent episodes of dark, tarry stools
options.C: Persistent fatigue and shortness of breath
options.D: Sudden uncontrollable muscle twitching

explanation: Spot on! Because anemic blood doesn't carry enough oxygen, the body's tissues lack fuel, leaving the patient feeling tired and breathless even with light activity.

question: What happens inside the eye if the fluid drainage gets blocked while the eye keeps making more fluid?

options.A: Eye pressure goes down
options.B: The ciliary body stops working
options.C: The cornea becomes completely opaque
options.D: Eye pressure goes up

explanation: Spot on! If fluid keeps pouring in but cannot flow out, it backs up and causes the pressure inside the eye to rise.

question: Which blood test result is a classic warning sign of severe internal poisoning from swallowed toxins?

options.A: An elevated platelet level
options.B: A high white blood cell count
options.C: A low serum sodium level
options.D: An increased anion gap

explanation: An increased anion gap tells you there is a buildup of hidden, dangerous acids circulating in the patient's blood.

question: What is another common name for the limbic system?

options.A: The emotional brain
options.B: The motor coordinator
options.C: The balance regulator
options.D: The thinking center

explanation: The limbic system is widely known as the emotional brain because it regulates moods, feelings, and basic survival instincts. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h1)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe belly pain and rectal bleeding after using a local herbal enema. What is the biggest nursing concern here?

options.A: Severe allergic rhinitis and upper airway swelling
options.B: Sudden complete obstruction of the upper esophagus
options.C: Trauma to the rectal mucosa and systemic toxicity
options.D: Immediate development of peripheral neuropathy

explanation: Harsh local enemas can easily tear the delicate lining of the rectum and quickly push strong, unmeasured chemicals straight into the bloodstream. Ouch! Patient safety is key here.

question: Why must nurses tailor assessment tools to fit a degenerative patient's physical limits?

options.A: To make the test results legally binding in a court of law
options.B: To eliminate the need for family members to be present
options.C: To ensure the patient does not get tired or frustrated during testing
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing paper questionnaires

explanation: If a patient is exhausted, test scores won't show their true ability. Matching their energy levels keeps the assessment accurate and stress-free.

question: A patient presents to the emergency ward with dry skin, a very high fever, blurry vision, and dilated pupils after taking an unknown medication. Which toxidrome is this?

options.A: Anticholinergic
options.B: Sympathomimetic
options.C: Cholinergic
options.D: Opioid

explanation: The classic presentation of dry skin, fever, confusion, and dilated pupils points directly to an anticholinergic poisoning syndrome. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why do patients need a broad support network during rehabilitation?

options.A: Families prefer to shift all medical duties to non-governmental groups
options.B: Hospitals lack the space to house recovering patients for more than a week
options.C: Doctors cannot manage chronic conditions without government supervision
options.D: Recovery continues long after hospital discharge and requires help from many sources

explanation: Healing doesn't stop just because the patient goes home. Family, community, and healthcare teams all team up to keep the momentum going!

question: According to Kübler-Ross, what is usually the first stage of grief?

options.A: Bargaining
options.B: Depression
options.C: Acceptance
options.D: Denial

explanation: You got it! Denial acts as a mental shock absorber, helping the mind ease slowly into accepting a painful reality.

question: Why is a clean cloth or gauze used between the skin and the poultice paste?

options.A: To keep the application neat and hold the paste together
options.B: To cure the infection without using any medicine
options.C: To completely block all heat from reaching the patient
options.D: To prevent the nurse from wearing clean gloves

explanation: The cloth acts as a barrier that contains the messy paste while allowing warmth and medicinal properties to pass through. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why must you let the alcohol skin cleanser dry completely before giving an intradermal injection?

options.A: To stop stinging pain caused by wet alcohol entering the puncture
options.B: To prevent the antiseptic from neutralizing the medication
options.C: To make the outer skin layer tough enough for the needle
options.D: To ensure the skin surface remains completely sterile

explanation: Thinking like a caring nurse! Letting the alcohol dry saves your patient from a sharp, unnecessary burning pain when the needle goes in.

question: Which type of cancer risk is actually lowered by long-term use of combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Stomach cancer
options.B: Ovarian cancer
options.C: Skin cancer
options.D: Lung cancer

explanation: By resting the ovaries and stopping ovulation over time, birth control pills actually help protect against ovarian and endometrial cancers. A nice little bonus benefit!

question: When should a puncture-resistant safety box for used syringes be sealed and prepared for disposal?

options.A: When it is filled up to the three-quarters mark
options.B: At the end of every working hour regardless of volume
options.C: When every single inch to the absolute brim is packed
options.D: Only when an external supervisor visits the clinic

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters prevents overfilling and lowers the risk of accidental punctures from protruding needles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: What is the medical term for a severe infection located right inside the bone tissue?

options.A: Nonunion
options.B: Compartment syndrome
options.C: Avascular necrosis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteo means bone, and myelitis refers to the marrow/infection. Put them together, and you get osteomyelitis—a stubborn bone infection that needs aggressive treatment.

question: In a standard three-chamber chest tube setup, what is the job of the very first chamber?

options.A: To filter out all bacteria entering from the room air
options.B: To add sterile water directly into the patient's lung tissue
options.C: To control the exact wall suction pressure applied to the unit
options.D: To collect and measure fluid draining from the patient

explanation: Chamber one is simply the catch basin. It safely collects whatever fluid, blood, or pus drains out so you can measure it easily.

question: What are the three core parts of the famous epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Source, vector, and cure
options.B: Bacteria, virus, and parasite
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Infection, symptom, and recovery

explanation: Never forget the classic trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (the surroundings). You've got this memorized now!

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive fresh vegetables you recommended. What is your best response?

options.A: Explore budget-friendly local produce or frozen vegetable alternatives
options.B: Advise them to spend less money on entertainment to buy groceries
options.C: Insist that fresh organic food is the only way to heal their body
options.D: Tell the patient to skip vegetables entirely and take a multivitamin

explanation: Well done! Nursing care has to fit the patient's pocket. Finding affordable local options keeps healthy eating realistic.

question: Why is cellular differentiation so important for the human body?

options.A: It ensures that all cells in the body remain identical
options.B: It stops normal cells from resting
options.C: It allows basic cells to mature into specific functional cells
options.D: It keeps the immune system calm

explanation: Brilliant! Differentiation is how a simple stem cell becomes a specialized muscle, nerve, or blood cell to do specific jobs in the body.

question: Why are pencil-point spinal needles often preferred over cutting needles?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of infection
options.B: They are cheaper to manufacture
options.C: They inject medication twice as fast
options.D: They separate dura fibers rather than cutting them

explanation: Pencil-point needles part the dural fibers, lowering the amount of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and reducing headache risks. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT part of an active drug history?

options.A: Past allergies or reactions to the substance
options.B: The dose and how often the drug is taken
options.C: The patient's childhood immunization record
options.D: The exact brand or generic name of the drug

explanation: Immunizations are part of the general medical history, not an active daily drug history. Every question you answer makes clinical practice clearer!

question: An older resident taking blood pressure pills suddenly feels dizzy and takes a fall. What should the nurse think of first?

options.A: An immediate need to discharge the resident home.
options.B: The complete absence of any pharmacological influence.
options.C: A normal reaction that requires no clinical follow-up.
options.D: A potential adverse drug reaction or cumulative medication effect.

explanation: Dizziness and sudden falls in older adults are classic clues that a medication might be lowering their blood pressure too much or making them drowsy.

question: Why do hospital leaders or administrators sometimes push back against health advocacy efforts?

options.A: Because advocacy always improves hospital finances instantly
options.B: Because community members demand too many medications
options.C: Because changes may threaten established budgets and power dynamics
options.D: Because nurses lack basic clinical training certificates

explanation: Exactly. Change can be scary for management if it means spending extra money or shaking up how things are normally done.

question: Why must you as a nurse pay attention to a patient's feelings and emotional triggers during nutrition counselling?

options.A: Patients cannot digest food properly when they are sad
options.B: Psychology is the only valid study of human health
options.C: It allows the nurse to diagnose mental illness
options.D: Emotional habits can sabotage even the best meal plans

explanation: So true! If we only hand out diet charts and ignore the emotional side of eating, the patient will likely struggle with overeating no matter how motivated they look.

question: How often should you check the baby's heartbeat during the second stage of normal labour?

options.A: Every 5 minutes
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Only after delivery

explanation: During pushing (stage two), there's a lot of pressure! Checking every 5 minutes helps us catch any signs of distress immediately.

question: What is usually the most important factor in keeping a synovial joint stable?

options.A: Length of the bones
options.B: Thickness of the skin
options.C: Muscle tone
options.D: Amount of synovial fluid

explanation: Well done! The constant, healthy tension in the muscles surrounding a joint (muscle tone) is what keeps everything safely in place.

question: What condition involves widespread, abnormal blood clotting followed by severe bleeding due to used-up clotting factors?

options.A: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
options.D: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

explanation: DIC is a serious complication where small clots form throughout the body, eventually exhausting clotting proteins and causing severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is newborn screening so important for babies with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It prevents the spleen from ever being damaged by blocked blood vessels
options.B: It stops red blood cells from ever changing into a crescent shape
options.C: It allows early penicillin prophylaxis and vaccination before severe infections occur
options.D: It cures the genetic mutation completely before symptoms start to show

explanation: Early detection saves lives! Finding the condition early lets doctors start daily penicillin and special vaccines right away, protecting the baby from dangerous infections.

question: What is the most frequent cause of nephrotic syndrome in young children?

options.A: Membranous nephropathy
options.B: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.C: Minimal change disease
options.D: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis

explanation: Minimal change disease accounts for the vast majority of nephrotic syndrome cases in children and usually responds very well to steroid therapy. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h2)

question: If a patient has a shorter-than-normal fallopian tube, what are the two main ways this can happen?

options.A: Hormonal or mechanical
options.B: Congenital or acquired
options.C: Primary or secondary ischemic
options.D: Infectious or malignant

explanation: Short tubes are either congenital (meaning present from birth due to development) or acquired later in life from things like scar tissue or surgery.

question: Which of these is NOT something food safety regulations normally check for?

options.A: Physical objects like metal shards or stones
options.B: Dangerous levels of chemical pesticide residues
options.C: Political views of the food manufacturing company owners
options.D: Harmful germs causing foodborne illnesses

explanation: Food safety is strictly about biological, chemical, and physical hazards—not who owns the company or what they believe!

question: Why do blood disorders like sickle cell anaemia often cause deep emotional distress for patients?

options.A: Because of the unpredictable pain crises and lifelong nature of the illness
options.B: Because daily physical therapy is strictly mandatory for everyone
options.C: Because patients get a quick and complete cure in most hospitals
options.D: Because there are never any physical symptoms during early stages

explanation: Living with a chronic condition that flares up unexpectedly takes a heavy mental toll. Understanding this helps you support the whole patient, not just their labs!

question: During antenatal clinic visits, which physical measurement is commonly used to track how the baby is growing?

options.A: Abdominal girth
options.B: Maternal weight gain
options.C: Pelvic diameter
options.D: Fundal height

explanation: Correct! Measuring the distance in centimeters from the pubic bone to the top of the uterus helps midwives and nurses check if the baby is growing right on track.

question: Which of these is NOT a red flag symptom that requires medical investigation? (Find the exception)

options.A: Occasional mild bloating after eating beans
options.B: Persistent, severe abdominal pain
options.C: Presence of blood in the stool
options.D: Unexplained and rapid weight loss

explanation: A little bloating after beans is completely normal! Blood, weight loss, and severe pain are the warning signs that need a doctor's attention.

question: A patient asks why their new medicine isn't making them feel better right away, even though the doctor says it's working. What should you tell them?

options.A: The patient must be taking the wrong dose for their weight
options.B: Medications only work if you drink lots of cold water with them
options.C: Disease-modifying drugs focus on slowing future damage rather than instant relief
options.D: The drug is probably fake and should be thrown away

explanation: Well done! It's completely normal for patients to feel confused by this. Remind them that these medications are playing the long game—protecting their future health rather than giving an instant energy boost.

question: What is the main job of the testes in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Secreting alkaline seminal fluid
options.B: Regulating scrotal skin moisture
options.C: Producing sperm and testosterone
options.D: Storing mature sperm cells

explanation: Spot on! The testes are the primary male organs responsible for making both testosterone (the male hormone) and sperm cells. You've got this!

question: Who should be involved when setting rehabilitation goals for a patient with a degenerative disorder?

options.A: Only the physical therapist and the patient
options.B: The healthcare team, the patient, and their family
options.C: Only the doctor and the hospital administrator
options.D: The insurance provider and the nursing supervisor

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Effective goal setting requires input from everyone involved in the patient's care to ensure targets are realistic and meaningful.

question: What is the main difference between droplet and airborne germs?

options.A: Airborne germs only spread outdoors
options.B: Airborne germs cannot infect healthcare workers
options.C: Droplet germs need negative pressure rooms
options.D: Droplet germs travel on heavy particles that fall quickly, while airborne germs stay floating longer

explanation: Think of it by weight! Heavier droplets drop fast to the ground, but tiny airborne particles float around longer and need stronger masks.

question: What is the medical term for when a child starts going through puberty much earlier than normal?

options.A: Hypogonadism
options.B: Precocious puberty
options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Delayed puberty

explanation: Great job! 'Precocious' means developing certain talents or traits earlier than expected—in this case, early puberty.

question: Why is 'dissemination' an important step in surveillance?

options.A: It stops patients from visiting primary health care clinics.
options.B: It permanently deletes old health records to save computer space.
options.C: It ensures feedback is shared with the workers and leaders who need to take action.
options.D: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies make a profit.

explanation: Dissemination just means sharing the news back. It closes the loop so the people who collected the data and the ones who need to fight the disease are on the same page!

question: A research group finds a questionnaire that was super reliable in the US ten years ago. Why must they test its reliability again for a new local study?

options.A: Hospital ethics committees require a new test to pay the researchers
options.B: Published research papers automatically expire after five years
options.C: Cultural differences and demographics can change how the tool performs
options.D: Statistical formulas change every decade to match new computer systems

explanation: Reliability isn't a permanent stamp of approval. A tool that works great in one culture or setting might need re-testing to prove it fits a different local population.

question: What is the main thing you do during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Gathering initial demographic data during the patient's admission
options.B: Writing out shift handoff notes without checking patient progress
options.C: Comparing the patient's actual health status against the expected outcomes
options.D: Formulating brand new medical diagnoses for the physician to sign

explanation: Evaluation is like checking your scorecard. You look back at the goals you set and ask, 'Did our care help the patient reach them?'

question: At what point must the surgical time-out be done?

options.A: When the patient first arrives at the hospital gate
options.B: During the patient discharge counseling session
options.C: Just before the surgical incision is made
options.D: After the surgical wound has been fully closed

explanation: The time-out is our final safety pause right before the knife touches the skin, giving the whole team a chance to confirm everything is correct.

question: What is the medical term for the procedure where the vaginal opening is narrowed by sealing the cut labia?

options.A: Infibulation
options.B: Excision
options.C: Cauterization
options.D: Clitoridectomy

explanation: Type III FGM, also known as infibulation, involves creating a seal over the vaginal opening using the labia. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the biggest benefit of connecting a newly injured patient with a peer support group?

options.A: Speeding up bone healing through group social activities
options.B: Learning practical coping tips from others who share similar experiences
options.C: Replacing the need for professional medical nursing care entirely
options.D: Ensuring the patient never feels sad or angry about the injury

explanation: You nailed it! Peer mentors offer real-world advice and encouragement that textbooks just can't match.

question: Which type of grasping instrument is safest to use on delicate organs like the bowel?

options.A: Non-toothed smooth forceps
options.B: Sharp bone-holding clamps
options.C: Toothed Adson forceps
options.D: Heavy locking Allis forceps

explanation: Smooth forceps lack sharp teeth, preventing them from puncturing or tearing fragile internal organs during manipulation. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why should a nurse know the difference between normal aging and an actual disease?

options.A: To prove that old age can be completely cured by medication
options.B: To reduce the overall cost of growing old
options.C: To ensure the patient qualifies for federal financial support
options.D: To avoid giving unnecessary medical treatments for normal body changes

explanation: Spot on! Recognizing normal body changes helps you avoid panicking or giving unnecessary treatments for things that are just part of growing older naturally.

question: What is the medical term for pain or a burning feeling when passing urine?

options.A: Polyuria
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Dysuria
options.D: Proteinuria

explanation: Dysuria is a word you'll use all the time in clinicals. 'Dys-' means painful or difficult, and '-uria' refers to urine!

question: During which phase of the heartbeat cycle does most blood flow into the heart muscle itself?

options.A: Systole
options.B: Isovolumetric contraction
options.C: Diastole
options.D: Atrial depolarization

explanation: You got this! When the heart relaxes during diastole, the squeezing pressure drops, allowing blood to finally rush freely into the coronary vessels.

question: Which professional helps residents adapt their living spaces to prevent falls and keep moving safely?

options.A: Hospital billing accountant
options.B: Facility maintenance engineer
options.C: Occupational or physiotherapist
options.D: Clinical research pharmacist

explanation: Spot on! Therapists are experts at checking physical ability and recommending exercises or environmental changes to stop falls.

question: What is the main goal of monitoring a patient after giving them a medication?

options.A: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay
options.B: To evaluate therapeutic effectiveness and watch for adverse reactions
options.C: To write a long essay about the patient's medical history
options.D: To prove to hospital management that nurses are working hard

explanation: Checking on your patient later lets you see if the drug is actually working and helps you catch any side effects early.

question: Why would you choose a subcutaneous injection instead of an IV for certain drugs like insulin?

options.A: To make the drug work instantly throughout the body
options.B: To bypass the need for a sterile syringe
options.C: To prevent any local skin irritation
options.D: To achieve a slow, sustained absorption rate

explanation: Spot on! Fatty tissue has fewer blood vessels than veins or muscles, which helps drugs like insulin release slowly and steadily into the body.

question: Which nutrient is most often missing in unfortified gluten-free grain alternatives?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: B vitamins
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Standard wheat products are usually fortified with B vitamins like folate, which alternative flours often lack unless added back.

question: How does Maslow's hierarchy of needs apply to nursing school and patient care?

options.A: Basic survival and safety needs must be met before higher learning occurs
options.B: Classroom lectures should always focus on physical punishment
options.C: Students must memorize every medical diagnosis before touching a patient
options.D: Emotional support is completely secondary to technical skills

explanation: It's hard to focus on studying pathophysiology if you're exhausted, starving, or stressed about safety. Basic needs always come first for both students and patients!

question: What is the main purpose of translating a community problem into a formal nursing diagnosis?

options.A: To replace all medical doctors in the primary healthcare center
options.B: To hide community health failures from government inspectors
options.C: To increase the cost of health services for local residents
options.D: To bridge data collection and structure a focused, goal-oriented care plan

explanation: A formal nursing diagnosis turns raw findings into a clear statement that guides planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is the legal status of treating medical complications from an abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: It is strictly forbidden unless authorized by a high court judge
options.B: It is a legal and medically necessary life-saving intervention
options.C: It is classified as an elective cosmetic procedure
options.D: It is only permitted in federal tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Saving a patient's life by treating emergency complications is always legal and always the top priority in healthcare.

question: What serious brain complication can happen when a drug overdose goes untreated and cuts off the body's oxygen supply for too long?

options.A: Rapid bone mineralization
options.B: Anoxic brain injury
options.C: Improved cognitive function
options.D: Enhanced muscle strength

explanation: When breathing slows down dangerously and isn't corrected, the brain gets starved of oxygen, which can unfortunately lead to permanent brain damage.

question: What happens in the colon when someone doesn't drink enough water?

options.A: Peristalsis becomes dangerously fast and watery
options.B: Gastric acid production increases rapidly
options.C: The colon extracts more water, causing hard and dry stool
options.D: The colon stops absorbing nutrients completely

explanation: When the body is short on water, the colon tries to save every drop by sucking extra moisture out of the waste, leading to dry, hard stools.

question: What makes an adverse drug reaction (ADR) different from a medication error?

options.A: An ADR happens even when the correct dose and drug are given.
options.B: An ADR is caused by the pharmacist giving the wrong medication.
options.C: An ADR only occurs if the nurse administers the drug too fast.
options.D: An ADR only happens during an intentional drug overdose.

explanation: You've got this! An ADR happens unexpectedly even when you do everything right with the dose and drug, unlike a dosage mistake.

question: A patient with a head injury has one pupil that is large and doesn't react well to light. What does this usually suggest?

options.A: An allergic reaction to systemic intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.B: A minor scalp laceration healing normally without complication
options.C: Compression of cranial nerve III due to brain herniation
options.D: Permanent regeneration of damaged peripheral nerve pathways

explanation: When pressure pushes brain tissue downward, it can squeeze cranial nerve III, which controls the pupil. This causes that classic 'fixed and dilated' pupil.

question: A patient tests negative for an STI just three days after a risky exposure. What crucial advice must you give them?

options.A: Antibiotics should still be taken immediately to prevent future infections
options.B: No further precautions are necessary because the immune system has cleared it
options.C: The test may be a false negative due to the window period, so a repeat test is needed
options.D: A negative result means the client is permanently immune to this specific pathogen

explanation: Remember the window period! It takes time for the body to build up enough markers for tests to spot them. Testing too early can give a false sense of safety.

question: What is the main purpose of an advanced healthcare directive?

options.A: To permit nurses to alter medical prescriptions independently
options.B: To guarantee financial compensation for hospital admission
options.C: To guide medical treatment choices before a patient loses the ability to decide
options.D: To protect the hospital from paying taxes on equipment

explanation: You nailed it! Advanced directives let people state their medical wishes ahead of time just in case they can't speak later.

question: When should a nurse teach a client to apply cold packs rather than heat to an arthritic joint?

options.A: Right before starting a long walk or stretching routine
options.B: After physical activity when the joint feels swollen and inflamed
options.C: Only when the weather turns very cold outside
options.D: First thing in the morning when the joint feels stiff

explanation: Cold helps constrict blood vessels and numb acute swelling after use, whereas heat is better for relaxing stiff muscles beforehand. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: A patient with bad food poisoning keeps throwing up and cannot keep any water down. What is your next best step?

options.A: Force the patient to drink large volumes of water
options.B: Withhold all fluids for the next 48 hours
options.C: Administer strong oral laxatives immediately
options.D: Initiate prescribed intravenous fluid therapy

explanation: If the mouth isn't an option because of constant vomiting, setting up an IV line is the safest way to get fluids and electrolytes back into their system.

question: Why is respite care recommended for family members caring for an Alzheimer's patient?

options.A: It teaches the patient how to live independently in their own home
options.B: It gives the primary caregiver temporary relief and rest from daily duties
options.C: It provides a permanent cure for the patient's behavioral issues
options.D: It permanently transfers all legal responsibility to the medical facility

explanation: Exactly right! Respite care gives families a short break to rest and protect their own health so they can keep providing loving care. Well done!

question: When is the best time to put lotion or moisturizer on the skin?

options.A: Right before taking a hot shower or bath
options.B: Exclusively before going to sleep at night
options.C: Immediately after bathing while the skin is still damp
options.D: Only when the skin begins to crack and bleed

explanation: You got it! Putting cream on slightly damp skin traps that moisture right where you want it, keeping dryness far away.

question: What is typically one of the earliest physical signs of significant blood loss?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing
options.B: Warm, flushed skin
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Fast heart rate

explanation: Tachycardia (fast heart rate) is the body's quick fix to keep blood moving when total volume starts to dip. You're mastering trauma basics!

question: What happens to the air left in the lungs after a normal breath (residual volume) as pregnancy advances?

options.A: It fluctuates wildly
options.B: It doubles
options.C: It decreases
options.D: It stays the same

explanation: Because the growing uterus pushes up, there is less room for leftover air trapped in the lungs after breathing out. You are learning fast!

question: What is the main job of the trophoblast layer during early development?

options.A: Producing red blood cells for the early embryo
options.B: Forming the central nervous system of the fetus
options.C: Burrowing into the uterine lining for implantation
options.D: Creating the outer skin layers of the baby

explanation: Correct! The trophoblast acts like a pioneer, helping the tiny embryo safely implant into the wall of the womb to build the placenta.

question: What is the primary focus of Prong 2 in the WHO PMTCT strategy?

options.A: Screening male partners for sexually transmitted diseases
options.B: Providing emergency formula milk to all mothers
options.C: Treating opportunistic infections in newborn infants
options.D: Preventing unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV

explanation: Prong 2 focuses on family planning and reproductive health services to help women living with HIV avoid unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: What is the biggest hurdle when trying to treat brain tumors using regular systemic chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: Chemotherapy drugs only work on bones and muscles.
options.B: Chemotherapy causes permanent blindness in every patient.
options.C: Brain tissue absorbs too much medication and dissolves instantly.
options.D: The blood-brain barrier blocks many drugs from entering the brain tissue.

explanation: You got it! The blood-brain barrier is like a strict security guard—it protects the brain from toxins, but unfortunately, it also blocks many helpful chemotherapy drugs from getting inside.

question: How can nurses safely manage IV fluids when electronic infusion pumps aren't available?

options.A: By using gravity drip sets paired with frequent manual monitoring of flow rates
options.B: By clamping the intravenous line completely shut for hours at a time
options.C: By squeezing the intravenous fluid bag continuously by hand until empty
options.D: By substituting all intravenous therapy with oral water ingestion

explanation: Gravity infusion sets plus regular, careful checks help nurses control flow safely even without fancy hospital equipment.

question: Why does injecting local numbing medicine directly into the middle of an inflamed abscess often not work very well?

options.A: The acidic environment of the pus neutralizes the local anesthetic
options.B: The nerve endings in the center are already permanently destroyed
options.C: The pus pressure pushes the medication back out the needle hole
options.D: The thick skin blocks the numbing medicine from spreading
