explanation: Infected, pus-filled areas have an acidic chemistry that stops the numbing medicine from doing its job. That is why doctors usually numb the healthy skin around the edges instead!

question: What is the main goal when doing rehabilitation care for older adults?

options.A: Accelerating the normal aging process in the body
options.B: Curing all chronic illnesses present in the patient
options.C: Maximizing the patient's independence and function
options.D: Providing permanent custodial nursing home placement

explanation: You're doing great! Gerontological rehab is all about helping older adults do as much as they can for themselves, rather than just chasing a cure for old age. Keep it up!

question: Why do intramuscular (IM) injections absorb faster than subcutaneous ones?

options.A: Muscle tissue has a much richer blood supply
options.B: The skin barrier is thinner over muscle sites
options.C: Injections into muscle bypass the liver completely
options.D: Needles used for muscle are always smaller

explanation: Think of blood vessels as busy highways! Because muscles have way more blood vessels than fatty tissue underneath the skin, the medicine gets swept right up into the bloodstream much faster.

question: What is the correct compression-to-breath ratio for single-rescuer adult CPR?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.C: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: The golden rule for adult BLS is 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. You'll memorize this in no time!

question: What is the main function of the LGA PHC Development Committee?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines for the entire country
options.B: Treating emergency trauma cases at teaching hospitals
options.C: Designing the national university medical curriculum
options.D: Allocating resources and coordinating health services across the entire local government

explanation: The LGA committee oversees all primary health care activities within its local government area, ensuring fair distribution of resources and personnel. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h4)

question: In the handy PQRSTU pain assessment tool, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

options.A: Quietness
options.B: Quantity
options.C: Quickness
options.D: Quality

explanation: Easy peasy! 'Q' stands for quality—asking the patient what the pain actually *feels* like (e.g., stabbing, dull, aching, or burning).

question: What happens right after a single sperm successfully enters an egg?

options.A: The placenta starts producing progesterone
options.B: The embryo immediately implants into the ovary
options.C: The mother's hormone levels drop sharply
options.D: The egg blocks other sperm from entering

explanation: Smart egg! To keep everything balanced, the egg instantly changes its outer layer so no other sperm can squeeze in.

question: Why would a patient need a triple-lumen catheter for continuous bladder irrigation?

options.A: It increases the French size automatically during surgery
options.B: It provides separate channels for drainage, balloon inflation, and fluid instillation
options.C: It prevents the patient from accidentally pulling the tube out
options.D: It allows three nurses to flush the bladder simultaneously

explanation: Exactly! Three separate pathways mean fluid can flow in, urine can flow out, and the balloon stays inflated all at the same time.

question: Which clinical encounter offers nurses a key opportunity to identify victims of early marriage?

options.A: Annual hospital administration meetings
options.B: Surgical safety checklist briefings
options.C: Routine occupational health screenings
options.D: Antenatal and maternity clinic visits

explanation: Young pregnant girls frequently interact with maternity nurses, making prenatal clinics ideal settings for identifying underage and coerced unions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h5)

question: How does the endocrine system compare to the nervous system when it comes to response time?

options.A: It relies exclusively on electrical nerve impulses
options.B: It produces slower, longer-lasting responses
options.C: It produces faster, short-lived responses
options.D: It only functions during times of acute physical trauma

explanation: While the nervous system acts like a quick text message (fast and brief), the endocrine system acts more like a long letter—it takes a bit longer to arrive, but the effect sticks around much longer!

question: Which blood type is known as the universal red blood cell donor because it has no A or B antigens?

options.A: Type O
options.B: Type A
options.C: Type AB
options.D: Type B

explanation: Correct! Because Type O red blood cells don't carry A or B antigens, a recipient's immune system won't easily attack them during emergencies.

question: Why are older adults much more likely to experience bad side effects from medications?

options.A: They always forget to swallow their pills with water
options.B: Their stomach acid completely destroys all medications
options.C: Their bodies metabolize and excrete medications much slower
options.D: They prefer taking herbal remedies instead of real drugs

explanation: Because liver and kidney functions slow down with age, drugs hang around in the body much longer. If doses aren't adjusted, they can easily build up to toxic levels.

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient gets a chemical splash in their eye?

options.A: Put in neutralizing acid drops to balance the pH
options.B: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop spreading
options.C: Cover the eye with a dry cotton pad and wait
options.D: Flush the eye continuously with clean water or saline for 15 to 30 minutes

explanation: Time is everything with chemical splashes! Wash it out immediately with lots of clean water or saline to protect the cornea from lasting damage.

question: Why might a nurse choose dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave for certain sharp tools or powders?

options.A: Dry heat uses steam pressure to penetrate thick plastic wrappers
options.B: Dry heat takes only two minutes to complete a full cycle
options.C: Dry heat is much cheaper to operate than electricity
options.D: Dry heat does not cause rusting or damage to moisture-sensitive items

explanation: Steam can rust fine metal edges or ruin powders. Dry heat is a wonderful alternative when you need to avoid moisture!

question: Which lab test is our best friend for spotting heart muscle damage?

options.A: Serum creatinine
options.B: Troponin
options.C: Serum potassium
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: Troponin is a special protein found inside heart muscle. When the heart gets hurt, troponin leaks out into the bloodstream for us to spot on labs.

question: Which of the following is a classic physical sign of repeated abuse often seen during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Generalized joint swelling caused by normal aging processes
options.B: Clean surgical incisions from previous routine procedures
options.C: Bruises in various stages of healing across the body
options.D: Symmetrical rashes located strictly on the lower extremities

explanation: Different colors of bruises indicate injuries sustained at different times, which is a strong indicator of ongoing physical abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h2)

question: A doctor asks if a pregnant woman can safely take a certain antibiotic. What is your best first step as the nurse?

options.A: Gather details on the patient's exact gestational age and kidney function
options.B: Immediately tell the doctor that all antibiotics are dangerous in pregnancy
options.C: Refuse to answer because prescribing is outside the nursing scope
options.D: Look up the generic name in a pocket drug guide without asking further details

explanation: You got it! Patient details like pregnancy stage and kidney health completely change how a drug is used, so always gather background info first.

question: A nurse is positioning a woman on the delivery bed for a long second stage of labor. What action helps protect her joints?

options.A: Elevating the head of the bed to a complete vertical sitting position
options.B: Ensuring proper joint alignment and adding supportive padding
options.C: Tying the legs tightly together to prevent excessive spreading
options.D: Massaging the calf muscles vigorously every five minutes

explanation: Proper body alignment and extra padding prevent unnatural twisting on relaxed ligaments during long periods in awkward positions.

question: Why is hand hygiene considered the most important part of standard precautions?

options.A: It completely sterilizes the skin of the hands
options.B: It removes transient microorganisms picked up from surfaces
options.C: It eliminates the need for wearing medical gloves
options.D: It neutralizes airborne toxins before inhalation

explanation: Well done! Washing or sanitizing your hands physically washes away the hitchhiking germs you pick up from touching patients and equipment, stopping cross-contamination in its tracks.

question: When using Naegele's Rule to calculate an expected delivery date, what do you do to the months?

options.A: Subtract nine months
options.B: Add three months
options.C: Add six months
options.D: Subtract three months

explanation: You've got it! Naegele's Rule is simple: take the last period's first day, add 7 days, and subtract 3 months. Easy peasy!

question: Testicular cancer is most commonly diagnosed in which age group?

options.A: Young men aged 15 to 35
options.B: Middle-aged men aged 50 to 65
options.C: Pre-pubertal boys under 10
options.D: Elderly men over 75 years

explanation: Good to know! Unlike many other cancers, testicular cancer hits younger guys, which is why teaching self-exams to this group is so vital.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's natural thermostat?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The hypothalamus

explanation: You got this! The hypothalamus acts as our internal thermostat, carefully keeping our core body temperature just right.

question: Why is keeping accurate and timely nursing notes so important in peri-operative care?

options.A: It allows the patient to perform their own dressing changes.
options.B: It provides a clear legal record of the care provided.
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shifts.
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital receives full financial grants.

explanation: Good medical records act as legal proof in court, showing that you delivered safe, standard care at the right time.

question: What is anticipatory grief?

options.A: Anger directed at doctors after a misdiagnosis
options.B: Depression caused by a sudden physical injury
options.C: Grief experienced before the actual death occurs
options.D: Relief felt when a patient finally passes away

explanation: Anticipatory grief is the mourning process that happens prior to an expected death as losses accumulate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: Which neonatal complication is commonly linked to fetal hyperinsulinemia delaying lung maturation?

options.A: Respiratory distress syndrome
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Necrotizing enterocolitis

explanation: High insulin levels can delay the production of lung surfactant, putting the newborn at a higher risk for respiratory distress syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h7)

question: How do medications interact with our cells?

options.A: By permanently replacing vital organs with chemical substitutes
options.B: By modifying or blocking already existing cellular activities
options.C: By changing the basic genetic code of the target organ
options.D: By destroying diseased cells and generating brand new tissues

explanation: Great job! Think of drugs as little keys that speed up, slow down, or block processes your body already knows how to do.

question: What is the main job of the motor areas in the brain's cerebral cortex?

options.A: Interpreting sounds and spoken language
options.B: Storing long-term episodic memories
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Processing visual images from the eyes

explanation: You've got this! The motor areas are specially designed to plan and make happen all the voluntary movements your body makes every day.

question: What is the most critical and life-threatening complication of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Permanent loss of the patient's voice and hearing
options.B: Sudden development of adult-onset type 1 diabetes
options.C: Tubal rupture and severe internal hemorrhage
options.D: Chronic swelling of the lower legs and feet

explanation: When the fallopian tube bursts from a growing ectopic pregnancy, it causes heavy internal bleeding that can quickly lead to shock and death if untreated. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h8)

question: Which piece of PPE is primarily used to protect the nurse's clothing from splashes of body fluids?

options.A: A surgical mask
options.B: Sterile shoe covers
options.C: A face shield
options.D: A protective gown

explanation: Gowns cover the uniform and skin of the torso to block fluid splashes during high-risk procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why do teenagers often take big risks even when they know it's dangerous?

options.A: They experience a permanent loss of short-term memory
options.B: They completely lack the ability to think logically
options.C: Their cognitive development stops entirely during puberty
options.D: Reward-seeking brain centers develop faster than impulse-control centers

explanation: The thrill-seeking part of the brain develops faster than the brake pedal (impulse control), making exciting experiences feel totally worth the risk to them.

question: What is the main characteristic of a 'just culture' in healthcare?

options.A: Allowing patients to manage their own hospital medication schedules
options.B: Punishing every single mistake severely regardless of the cause
options.C: Balancing individual accountability with systemic error analysis
options.D: Ignoring minor errors to keep staff morale high and positive

explanation: A just culture means you can speak up and report mistakes honestly without fear of unfair punishment, while still holding everyone reasonably accountable.

question: Which electrolyte is found mostly inside the cells and is vital for heart rhythm?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Chloride

explanation: Potassium is the chief intracellular cation, and even small changes in its level can dangerously disrupt heart rhythm. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why is the formation of a dense fibrin mesh essential for wound healing?

options.A: It dilutes the concentration of red blood cells near the injury
options.B: It speeds up the removal of waste products from damaged tissues
options.C: It lowers the local blood pressure to stop bleeding instantly
options.D: It reinforces the weak platelet plug into a strong, stable clot

explanation: The fibrin mesh acts like concrete scaffolding, locking the platelets and blood cells together into a sturdy patch that stops bleeding securely. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why can diagnosing an emerging infection be very difficult during the early stages?

options.A: Patients refuse to answer basic questions about their health
options.B: Laboratory equipment automatically destroys new viral samples
options.C: Early symptoms often look identical to common endemic illnesses
options.D: Fever never appears during the first week of any infection

explanation: Initial signs like fever, headache, and body aches are shared by many everyday diseases, making unique identification tricky at first. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a patient with an ovarian cyst should report right away?

options.A: A slight increase in clear vaginal discharge
options.B: Mild bloating right before her monthly period
options.C: Sudden, severe, and worsening abdominal pain
options.D: Feeling tired after a long day at work

explanation: Severe pain that comes out of nowhere is a red flag for dangerous complications like a cyst bursting or twisting (torsion). Always take it seriously!

question: What is the main nursing priority right after delivery for a patient who had placenta accreta?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of postpartum hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Administering oral iron supplements for mild fatigue
options.C: Encouraging immediate ambulation around the ward
options.D: Preparing the infant for immediate nursery discharge

explanation: Because accreta makes it hard for the uterus to contract properly and clear all tissue, keeping a close eye on bleeding is your number one lifesaving duty. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h8)

question: Which part of the nervous system is responsible for triggering a penile erection?

options.A: Somatic motor nervous system
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Central spinal nervous system

explanation: Well done! The parasympathetic nervous system handles the 'rest and digest' actions, including sending signals that relax blood vessels so erectile tissue can fill with blood.

question: Why is psychological safety so important for nurses on the ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to skip mandatory documentation and charting duties
options.B: It gives them the confidence to speak up about safety hazards without fear
options.C: It completely eliminates all physical stress and burnout on the ward
options.D: It prevents patients from asking difficult questions about their care

explanation: When nurses feel psychologically safe, they won't hesitate to question a dodgy doctor's order or report a near-miss, and that saves lives!

question: Two family members disagree sharply on whether to pursue aggressive treatment for a failing relative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Facilitate a structured family meeting to let both parties voice concerns
options.B: Choose one family member at random to make all the final decisions
options.C: Tell the family members they are not allowed to visit anymore
options.D: Ignore the family conflict and follow only the primary doctor's orders

explanation: A structured meeting allows family members to express their viewpoints safely and helps the care team work toward consensus. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a health screening test?

options.A: To replace a clinical doctor's formal diagnosis
options.B: To cure an advanced chronic illness permanently
options.C: To prevent the initial exposure to a pathogen
options.D: To find hidden disease before symptoms appear

explanation: Screening is designed to catch health problems early in people who feel well so that prompt treatment can begin. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h3)

question: You feel an organ extending past the left rib margin during a deep abdominal exam. What organ are you most likely feeling?

options.A: Kidney
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Spleen

explanation: The spleen hangs out in the upper left side of the abdomen. If it's enlarged, it extends downward from beneath the left ribs where you can feel it.

question: Why are alternative rites of passage considered effective grassroots strategies against FGM?

options.A: They replace traditional ceremonies with strict western religious rituals
options.B: They preserve cultural celebrations of maturity while eliminating physical harm
options.C: They allow traditional cutters to continue practicing safely in hospitals
options.D: They provide direct employment for healthcare workers in rural clinics

explanation: Alternative rites honor the cultural need for a coming-of-age milestone while removing the dangerous physical cutting component. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular diabetic complications?

options.A: If the condition affects the upper or lower body
options.B: Whether the patient feels pain or numbness
options.C: The size of the damaged blood vessels
options.D: How fast the symptoms appear after a meal

explanation: It's all in the name! Micro means tiny vessels (like in the eyes and kidneys), while macro means larger arteries (like heart and brain vessels).

question: What is a dual-chamber pacemaker designed to do?

options.A: Pace both an atrium and a ventricle
options.B: Store two separate batteries for emergencies
options.C: Pace the left and right lungs together
options.D: Monitor blood pressure and breathing rate

explanation: A dual-chamber system uses two leads to coordinate contractions in both upper and lower chambers of the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is considered the gold standard method for measuring energy expenditure in a clinical setting?

options.A: Indirect calorimetry
options.B: Standard height-weight charts
options.C: Bioelectrical impedance
options.D: Skinfold caliper testing

explanation: Indirect calorimetry is a neat clinical test that calculates metabolic rate by analyzing the oxygen a patient inhales and the carbon dioxide they exhale.

question: Why should parents praise a gifted child's hard work rather than their raw smarts?

options.A: To prevent the development of crippling perfectionism
options.B: To speed up asynchronous physical growth rates
options.C: To eliminate the need for specialized schooling
options.D: To guarantee university admission later in life

explanation: Praising effort teaches kids that it's okay to make mistakes and try again. Praising 'smartness' can make them terrified of failing later on. Beautiful learning moment!

question: Why is it usually a bad idea to use a young child or relative as an interpreter for complex medication instructions?

options.A: Using family members violates hospital financial accounting protocols
options.B: Family members may unintentionally omit or misinterpret complex medical details
options.C: Family members are legally barred from knowing medication dosages
options.D: Relative interpreters always make the patient feel more anxious than strangers

explanation: Loved ones want to help, but medical terms are tricky. They might miss vital dosage warnings by accident, so a trained interpreter is always safer.

question: What is the main difference between shear and friction in skin breakdown?

options.A: Shear only happens on the heels, whereas friction only happens on the sacrum.
options.B: Shear happens when bones slide inside while skin stays stuck; friction is just surface rubbing.
options.C: Shear damages bone tissue, whereas friction only damages hair follicles.
options.D: Shear is caused by moisture, whereas friction is caused by lack of protein.

explanation: Friction is like skin rubbing against bedsheets, but shear happens when the skeleton slides down while the outer skin stays put, twisting the blood vessels inside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the general long-term outlook for a patient who has a benign heart tumour completely removed?

options.A: Poor, with a life expectancy of only a few weeks
options.B: Hopeless without a full heart transplant
options.C: Guarded, because benign tumours always spread to the liver
options.D: Excellent, with most patients returning to normal activities

explanation: Once a benign tumour is successfully taken out, the cure rate is super high and patients usually get right back to their normal lives. Wonderful news for patients!

question: What is the medical term for when the tonsils get inflamed and swollen?

options.A: Laryngitis
options.B: Rhinitis
options.C: Tonsillitis
options.D: Pharyngitis

explanation: Correct! Tonsillitis simply means your tonsils are inflamed and fighting off an infection.

question: What part of a mature sperm cell contains the enzymes needed to penetrate an egg?

options.A: The acrosome
options.B: The midpiece
options.C: The nucleus
options.D: The flagellum

explanation: The acrosome sits atop the head of the sperm and releases digestive enzymes to break through the protective layers of the oocyte. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why must certain antiretroviral drugs be taken alongside food?

options.A: To stop the patient from feeling hungry at night
options.B: To replace drinking clean water
options.C: To reduce stomach irritation and improve drug absorption
options.D: To destroy the outer tablet coating instantly

explanation: You nailed it! Some meds are much easier on the stomach and work better when taken with a meal or snack.

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to understand basic X-ray imaging?

options.A: To replace the radiologist in reading films
options.B: To prescribe the correct radiation dosage
options.C: To operate the heavy X-ray machine safely
options.D: To help coordinate care and ease patient anxiety

explanation: As a nurse, you are the friendly face who prepares patients and calms their nerves before procedures. Great nursing starts with great communication!

question: Which imaging tool is usually used first to check for fluid in the Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Barium enema study
options.B: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.C: MRI scan
options.D: Plain abdominal X-ray

explanation: You've got this! A transvaginal ultrasound gives a clear, close-up look at pelvic structures and spots fluid pockets easily without surgery.

question: When should you as a nurse hold off on bladder irrigation unless the doctor specifically says it's okay?

options.A: When there is suspected trauma to the urinary tract
options.B: When urine output drops slightly over a two-hour window
options.C: When cloudy urine appears in the clear drainage tubing
options.D: When the patient reports mild burning around the meatus

explanation: Safety first! If the urinary tract is injured, pushing fluid in can force bacteria and fluid straight out into the pelvic tissue through the tear.

question: You notice two drugs with very similar names sitting right next to each other on the pharmacy shelf. What should you do?

options.A: Separate the look-alike sound-alike drugs to prevent future selection errors
options.B: Throw both medications straight into the general household trash bin
options.C: Mix them together in one container to save valuable shelf space
options.D: Leave them alone because pharmacy staff arranged the shelf originally

explanation: Spreading out look-alike, sound-alike drugs is a smart safety trick. It stops you or a colleague from grabbing the wrong box on a super busy shift!

question: What do we call the mild mood swings and crying spells many women feel in the first week after birth?

options.A: Baby blues
options.B: Puerperal fever
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Postpartum psychosis

explanation: Spot on! The 'baby blues' are very common and normal due to sudden hormone shifts. They usually pass on their own within two weeks with a little love and support.

question: Which nursing action helps thin thick respiratory secretions so they are easier for the patient to cough up?

options.A: Lying the patient flat on their back
options.B: Keeping the room air completely dry
options.C: Encouraging adequate daily fluid intake
options.D: Restricting all drinking water after meals

explanation: Drinking enough water keeps body fluids thin, which naturally loosens thick mucus in the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which part of the adolescent brain matures faster, leading to reward-seeking and impulsive behavior?

options.A: The limbic system
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The prefrontal cortex
options.D: The brainstem

explanation: The limbic system develops early during puberty, driving strong emotions and a desire for immediate rewards before the logical reasoning centers are fully mature. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h2)

question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely
options.B: The total absence of any bacteria or viruses in the pelvic organs
options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Think of reproductive health as more than just working body parts. The WHO looks at the whole person—physical, mental, and social well-being together!

question: What is the main reason we use stitches to close a simple skin cut?

options.A: To reduce healing time and minimize scarring
options.B: To stop deep muscle spasms near the injury site
options.C: To permanently eliminate all risk of bacterial infection
options.D: To replace the need for a tetanus toxoid booster

explanation: You've got this! Bringing the skin edges neatly together helps the cut heal much faster and keeps the scar as small as possible. Great job!

question: You check an ECG strip and see the spaces between the R waves are all over the place. Which step of your review does this fall under?

options.A: P wave morphology
options.B: ST segment elevation
options.C: Rhythm
options.D: PR interval duration

explanation: Checking if those R waves are marching evenly helps you figure out if the heart rhythm is regular or not.

question: Which nursing action provides the most accurate daily measurement of fluid retention in a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Asking the patient how tight their shoes feel each morning
options.B: Weighing the patient at the exact same time every day on the same scale
options.C: Measuring the abdominal girth with a soft tape measure once per shift
options.D: Counting how many times the patient asks to use the restroom

explanation: Daily weights using the same scale and clothing weight offer the most reliable data on whether fluid is accumulating or being successfully removed. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h5)

question: A choking patient suddenly passes out and falls to the floor. What should you do right away?

options.A: Start chest compressions and check the mouth for the object
options.B: Prepare to perform a surgical opening in the neck
options.C: Give an emergency injection of adrenaline
options.D: Prop the patient up in a high sitting position in bed

explanation: Once a choking victim collapses, you transition into CPR. Pumping the chest helps push air against the blockage, and you can check the mouth to scoop out the object if you see it.

question: What kind of data do you collect when running through the review of systems?

options.A: It documents surgical procedures performed in the past
options.B: It consists entirely of subjective data reported by the patient
options.C: It represents laboratory values collected from blood samples
options.D: It consists entirely of objective data measured by the nurse

explanation: You nailed it! Just like the rest of the history, this part is all about what the patient tells you they are experiencing.

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

options.A: Conducting annual financial audits for human resources
options.B: Designing new production machinery to eliminate safety hazards
options.C: Coordinating medical treatments and return-to-work plans for injured staff
options.D: Purchasing personal protective equipment for the entire industrial plant

explanation: Exactly! As case managers, nurses guide injured workers through their recovery and help them safely get back to work.

question: Because a pregnant teenager's pelvis is still growing, she is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Obstructed labor
options.B: Chronic heart failure
options.C: Placental overgrowth
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: You're doing great! An immature pelvis may not be wide enough for the baby to pass through easily, raising the risk of obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: Besides filtering waste and making urine, what other major job do the kidneys have?

options.A: Producing and releasing vital hormones
options.B: Storing bile for fat digestion
options.C: Manufacturing white blood cells
options.D: Synthesizing digestive enzymes

explanation: The kidneys double as endocrine organs that manufacture and release hormones directly into the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which brain structure kicks off the hormonal changes of puberty?

options.A: Anterior pituitary
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Pineal gland
options.D: Adrenal cortex

explanation: Spot on! The hypothalamus is the master control center that starts the whole process by releasing puberty hormones.

question: What is a major, life-threatening complication that can happen if bone infections are left untreated?

options.A: Permanent vision loss in both eyes
options.B: Total loss of stomach acid
options.C: Sepsis and septic shock
options.D: Sudden development of asthma

explanation: When an infection escapes the bone and enters the bloodstream, it can cause a whole-body emergency known as sepsis. Catching it early is key!

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

options.A: It represents the maximum depth of permanent skin and muscle destruction.
options.B: Infection rarely occurs in this specific layer of the burn wound.
options.C: This area is completely insensate and requires immediate surgical removal.
options.D: Tissue in this zone has reduced blood flow and can be saved from necrosis.

explanation: The zone of stasis is bruised and sluggish, but not dead yet! Quick fluids keep blood flowing there so it doesn't cross over into tissue death (necrosis). Great nursing care saves the day!

question: What is the purpose of taking a plain x-ray of the abdomen before injecting the contrast dye?

options.A: To test if the intravenous line is working properly
options.B: To measure the exact amount of urine currently in the bladder
options.C: To warm up the x-ray machine before the actual test begins
options.D: To check patient positioning and verify bowel preparation

explanation: The initial scout film confirms that the bowels are clean enough and that the x-ray machine is positioned correctly over the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h5)

question: What are the three main behaviors checked when scoring the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?

options.A: Reflexes, muscle tone, and pupil size
options.B: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.C: Sensory touch, pain, and temperature
options.D: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response

explanation: You've got this! The GCS looks at these three simple reactions to quickly check how well the brain is functioning.

question: What is a major challenge to good communication in busy Nigerian clinics?

options.A: The complete absence of cultural traditions
options.B: An oversupply of advanced diagnostic equipment
options.C: Heavy patient loads and understaffed facilities
options.D: Mandatory communication training for all staff

explanation: True! When clinics are overcrowded and nurses are rushed, it becomes so easy to slip into commanding or hurried communication.

question: How does a provoked seizure differ from epilepsy?

options.A: Provoked seizures require lifelong anti-seizure medication
options.B: Provoked seizures occur due to a temporary, acute trigger like low blood sugar
options.C: Provoked seizures are always generalized tonic-clonic events
options.D: Provoked seizures only happen during sleep cycles

explanation: A provoked seizure happens because of a temporary stressor on the body, such as high fever or low blood sugar, rather than a chronic brain condition. Great job thinking it through!

question: What is another common term for a congenital anomaly?

options.A: A degenerative illness
options.B: A birth defect
options.C: An infectious disease
options.D: An acquired injury

explanation: Congenital anomalies are physical or functional abnormalities present from birth, which is why they are commonly called birth defects. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h1)

question: A patient comes back two days after an abscess drainage with a fever and redness that is spreading outward from the wound. What does this mean?

options.A: Worsening infection requiring prompt medical reassessment
options.B: An allergic reaction to the cotton inside the dressing
options.C: Successful eradication of all bacteria from the body
options.D: Normal healing response as the deep tissues close

explanation: Spreading redness and fever are warning signs that the infection is fighting back and traveling further. The patient needs a doctor to take a look right away.

question: Which of the following is NOT a true barrier to assertive nursing practice?

options.A: Intimidation by experienced medical colleagues
options.B: Fear of being labeled as a difficult troublemaker
options.C: Having clear, updated hospital policies on safety
options.D: Cultural norms that discourage questioning seniors

explanation: Clear safety policies actually support and encourage nurses to speak up, rather than acting as a barrier. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you must check before helping someone who has collapsed?

options.A: Scene safety
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: The patient's pulse
options.D: Pupil reaction

explanation: Safety first! Always check that the environment is safe for you before rushing in to help. We need you safe too!

question: What is the main job of the skin as a body organ?

options.A: Filtering waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.B: Regulating the production of major digestive enzymes
options.C: Serving as a primary defense against pathogens and fluid loss
options.D: Producing red blood cells for systemic circulation

explanation: Great job! Think of your skin as your body's natural raincoat and security guard rolled into one—it keeps germs out and your precious body fluids in.

question: Which part of a normal ECG tracing shows the electrical recovery of the ventricles?

options.A: QRS complex
options.B: P wave
options.C: PR interval
options.D: T wave

explanation: The T wave is like the heart taking a deep breath and resetting its electrical charge after a hard squeeze, getting ready for the next beat.

question: How do our veins manage to push blood all the way back up to the heart against gravity?

options.A: By widening the tiny vessels in the capillary beds
options.B: Using the strong pumping push from the left side of the heart
options.C: Using muscle squeezes and tiny one-way valves inside
options.D: By sucking up fluid from surrounding tissues

explanation: Since blood pressure is low in veins, they need your leg and body muscles to squeeze them, plus built-in one-way valves that stop the blood from sliding backward. Brilliant work!

question: Which vitamin is most commonly recommended as a first-line supplement for pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin A
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B6

explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is a safe, go-to supplement prescribed in antenatal clinics to help ease that queasy feeling.

question: Why is getting the partner's approval emphasized so heavily during family planning counseling?

options.A: Ignoring it can lead to domestic conflict and discontinuation
options.B: The law requires men to test the medicine first
options.C: Husbands must sign a legal contract for every pill
options.D: Women are not allowed to touch medical items

explanation: Spot on! Without a husband's backing, women often face serious backlash at home and are forced to stop using their method.

question: What is the main purpose of giving a patient a purgative?

options.A: To increase the absorption of water in the large intestine
options.B: To slow down gastrointestinal motility and prevent diarrhea
options.C: To promote bowel movements and relieve constipation
options.D: To neutralize excess stomach acid and soothe ulcers

explanation: You've got this! Purgatives are simply given to help clear the bowels and get things moving when a patient is constipated.

question: Your catheterized patient has had no urine output for two hours and feels lower belly discomfort. What do you check first?

options.A: Check the tubing for kinks, twists, or compression under the patient
options.B: Call the doctor to report acute kidney failure
options.C: Remove the catheter immediately and insert a new one
options.D: Inject sterile water into the balloon to secure it further

explanation: Always look for the simple fix first! A twisted or flattened tube is usually the culprit when urine suddenly stops flowing.

question: How does severe malnutrition negatively impact a community's immune status?

options.A: It directly destroys the skin's physical ability to sweat
options.B: It prevents infants from absorbing breast milk antibodies
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which vaccines expire in storage
options.D: It impairs the body's ability to produce antibodies and immune cells

explanation: Nutrients are the building blocks of the immune system; lacking them stops the body from making enough cells and antibodies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why do we let patients try out a new physical skill themselves during teaching?

options.A: It ensures the patient can safely perform the task on their own
options.B: It is required to update the electronic health record
options.C: It prevents the patient from asking difficult questions
options.D: It makes the nurse finish their shift much faster

explanation: Brilliant! Having them practice physically builds their confidence and proves they can handle it safely once they go home.
